title: lighthouse-friction-snapshot-and-micro-probe-map-nov-2028
body:
TL;DR: Field teams have been flagging several recurring friction patterns tied to inference behaviour at scale. Many asks are small-scope changes or probes that could materially improve customer satisfaction with modest engineering effort. This doc compiles raw signals from calls and support threads (Nov 2028), synthesizes into micro-asks, and proposes 3 rapid probes + owners and metrics to validate impact.

Context + signal sources:
- Time window: customer support transcripts + CSM notes (2028-11-01 -> 2028-11-14). Primary sources: enterprise onboarding calls, Dedicated customer postmortems, a set of high-usage hosted API customers flagged in weekly CS sync.
- Representative threads: repeated mentions of "inconsistent latency when batch size spikes", "unexpected reroute to lower-capacity model variant", and "billing surprises from hidden retry tokens".
- Severity mix: ~60% UX friction (confusing fallbacks, opaque errors), ~30% operational risk (latency/regression on canaries), ~10% billing/contract/entitlement edge cases.

Raw customer quotes (verbatim snippets):
- "We saw a sudden jump in 95th latency after a marketing email — our traffic spiked and responses lagged. The fallback model produced lower-quality summaries and our PM noticed the change." — FinServ platform (Dedicated)
- "SDK retried silently and we got billed for duplicate tokens; we had to reconcile invoices and open a support ticket." — mid-market SaaS
- "Prefix caching is amazing, but when we changed prompt length distribution the cache miss rate exploded and throughput collapsed." — AI-native company

Top micro-asks (ranked by expected customer impact / low effort):
1) Fallback transparency toggle (impact: high, effort: low-medium)
   - What customers ask: ability to receive a structured event/log when a request is served by a fallback model or capacity tier (with model_id, reason code).
   - Proposed MVP: add a boolean query param /response_headers: fallback-reason + model-id in response metadata. Default off; opt-in via account setting.
   - Why high impact: reduces surprise, speeds incident triage, reduces CS load.
   - Quick metric: number of follow-ups per incident drop by 40% in pilot group.
   - Owner: Product (hosted-api) + Eng (runtime routing)

2) Retry billing audit endpoint (impact: medium, effort: low)
   - Ask: a simple audit log exposing retry events tied to original request ids for first-party SDKs; CSV export for finance teams.
   - MVP: expose endpoint /billing/audit/retries?start=... that returns [request_id, retry_count, tokens_charged, requester_account].
   - Why: prevents long reconciliation cycles; immediate customer delight for mid-market finance teams.
   - Owner: Finance + Billing infra; CS to pilot with 3 customers.

3) Lightweight cache-visibility probe (impact: high, effort: medium)
   - Ask: visibility into prefix/KV cache hit/miss rates per route during a timeslice. Customers want to correlate prompt changes to cache behavior.
   - MVP probe: add a per-route /observability/cache-stats endpoint sampling last 30 minutes: hit_rate, miss_rate, top-5 keys evicted.
   - Quick metric: pilot customers report faster root-cause time; should reduce support tickets about "throughput regression after prompt change".
   - Owner: Observability + Serving runtime

4) Canary-fallback policy audit trail (impact: medium, effort: medium)
   - Ask: why did canary choose to fallback — customers want an audit trail of policy decisions (scores, capacity thresholds).
   - MVP: structured decision trace in logs for canary rollouts (keep tiny — sampling possible).

5) Low-friction dev-tool: synthetic burst replayer (impact: medium, effort: low)
   - Small CLI that replays representative traffic spikes (preserving token distribution) into a test route so customers and SEs can reproduce behavior locally before production pushes.

Proposed experiments / probes (30-day cadence):
- Probe A (2 weeks): Rollout fallback-transparency to 5 pilot accounts (mix: hosted API + Dedicated). Measure CS ticket volume, incident survey NPS change, and number of times customers toggle setting.
- Probe B (2 weeks concurrent): Billing retry audit for two customers with prior billing disputes. Track time-to-resolution and finance-satisfaction survey.
- Probe C (4 weeks): Cache-visibility enabled for 3 customers; correlate cache stats with request traces and run two internal postmortems on one observed regression.

Priority matrix (quick view):
- Quick wins (1–2 weeks): Fallback transparency toggle, Retry billing audit, Synthetic burst CLI.
- Moderate (2–6 weeks): Cache-visibility probe, Canary audit traces.
- Major (quarter): Changes to automatic fallback routing logic, billing model rework, full observability UI panels.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Privacy: fallback metadata must not leak model internals or PII. Use standardized reason codes (e.g., CAPACITY_SHORTAGE, LATENCY_SLO_EVICTION, VERSION_MISMATCH).
- Performance: adding per-request headers should be carefully sampled for high-throughput routes to avoid overhead — we prefer opt-in account-level toggle.
- Billing audit: ensure logs can be queried by both finance and CS without exposing raw prompt content. Use request_id mapping only.

Suggested rollout & success metrics:
- Adoption: % customers who enable fallback-transparency within pilot cohort. Target: 50% within 2 weeks.
- Operational: mean time to root cause (MTTR) for incidents tied to fallback routing reduced by 30%.
- Business: decrease in billing dispute tickets related to retries by 80% for audited customers.

Open questions / risks:
- Will exposing fallback model-id encourage customers to bind to specific variants? Risk of customers using that to lock onto models outside our recommended variant map. Mitigation: provide guidance + sandbox docs.
- Storage and retention for retry audit logs — legal/finance may ask for longer retention. Need billing/legal input.
- Sampling policy: what fraction of requests should include verbose decision traces to balance observability vs. system overhead?

Next steps (owners + timeline):
- Week 0–1: Product to scope fallback header schema & reason codes (Priya Nair lead).
- Week 1–2: Eng (runtime) to implement opt-in response header + feature flag; small e2e test. (Eliot Zhou).
- Week 1–3: Billing infra to stand up audit endpoint & agree retention (Carlos Ramirez).
- Week 2–6: Observability to prototype cache-stats endpoint and run internal replay on synthetic spikes (Maya Singh).
- Week 3: CS to recruit 5 pilot customers and prepare communications + survey template (Lena Park).

Appendix: quick wire for fallback header (informal)
- Response metadata when enabled: {"fallback_used": "true|false", "fallback_model": "string|null", "fallback_reason_code": "CAPACITY_SHORTAGE|LATENCY_SLO_EVICTION|COMPATIBILITY"} — delivered as response header X-RW-Fallback: base64(json) or as SDK event for binary-safe transports.

Notes to self / todo for doc prep:
- Add anonymized incident excerpts (CS permission) before sending to eng.
- Confirm legal retention window for billing audit logs.
- Draft pilot customer email + opt-in form.

Bottom line: small, targeted visibility improvements (headers, audit endpoints, cache sampling) will likely deliver outsized reduction in customer confusion and support load. These are low-friction, measurable probes we can run in parallel and iterate on.

Document history: started 2028-11-17 (Lena Park), updated 2028-11-20 (added probe metrics and owners).
